comments.author: @sippigrrrl
comments.text:
10:01 I bought this exact same 2026 Integra Type S last year, and I actually was able to get it for $52K with the “ceramic window tint” but it took me waiting for them to call me back a week after I walked out. I had the money in my checking account and ready to go, but they didn’t want to give me the out the door price because I was buying it outright and I didn’t want to waste my time filling out the credit application and dealing with the hard sell tactics. It was hard to walk out because I really wanted it, but the sales manager called me a week later and I took my happy butt back to the dealership and refused to pay for the tint because I didn’t account for it in the total and I wasn’t going to do a separate transaction to pay for the tint. 

I love my new car, but I didn’t like that I had to pay taxes on the bitcoin I cashed in to pay for the car that had more than quintupled since I bought it. It put me into a different tax bracket. Oops, that’s my FAFO story about making a quasi-impulse $52K car purchase but at least I didn’t have to pay 7%+ APR for it. That’s the biggest investment I’ve made other than my homes, and I didn’t actually ask my husband, I just had a different car when I got home, and he kept my 2023 Civic for his daily driver. I guess I’m glad that I sold some of my bitcoin when I did because it’s crashed since 2025. I’m just lucky to be able to buy a new car, but the whole process is maddening and I really shouldn’t have been so ready to buy it from the dealer after they basically refused to remove the market adjustment the first time I went in, I just got excited because I’ve wanted some form of the Acura Integra Type R/S since 2003 or so, and I was finally able to get it now that I’m too old to really “drive it like I stole it” (as the saying goes). I might have clapped my hands and squealed very quietly when I finally got that key fob in my hot little hands!
